output.brief: Don't issue the breach notice. The rise in Corvane's missed bags is not a handler problem. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crew pool and stayed flat at about 3.6–3.8. Corvane's bags that were read automatically stayed at about 3.8. The whole increase is in bags sent to manual encoding. That volume went from about 70 to about 460 a day, and 91% of the encode-path bags that missed their flight reached the lateral after it closed. Tag read failures rose from 1.5% to 11.8% for Corvane tags printed on the new Fennick stock from 1 Sep. Corvane transfer tags and Pelion tags stayed at about 1.3–1.4%. On 14–16 Oct, counter tags printed on old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6%. Kiosk tags on Fennick stock failed at 12.1% the same days. So the stock change is the cause. The evidence doesn't show whether the Fennick stock is defective or the printer heat setting needs adjusting. Next steps: switch back to the Brackwater stock held in stores now, which is reversible and covers about five weeks. Meanwhile ask the printer maker and Fennick to settle whether it's the stock or the setting, and hold any defect claim until then. Ask HBAA for temporary extra encode capacity in the evening. Tell the VP that withholding Tessaly's fee would penalise the wrong party. Confidence is fairly high.
